Tree read: HEAD 7c77f3594, every file of this item clean. The mechanism, the family and every symbol name in the map hold up against the code. Six things need changing before a work order: (1) the recommended menu accelerator plus guide pair reddens a registered row the map does not list (GH6 of test_wave_grid, display arm); (2) the proposed pure decision proc will kill every graph key under NumLock unless it normalises the state the way callback() does; (3) the Caps Lock matrix row proposed for test_wave_subwindows can arm a schematic MOVE in the fixture viewer and can hang pre-fix; (4) the 20/15 literals live in more places than the map says; (5) two user-facing texts and the house "new viewer key" recipe are missing from the map; (6) issue number 1728 is taken by the private clone.

POPUP PATH, read end to end. wviewer::strip_bindings (src/wave_viewer.tcl) binds only <KeyPress>/<KeyRelease> -> wviewer::key_filter on the widget and puts WaveViewer right after the widget in bindtags (WvFszCanvas at index 0 carries no key binding). key_filter: wviewer::case_keysym keeps 77 at state 5 and maps 109 at state 6 to 77; 77 is in `variable graphkeys` {97 98 100 115 109 116 65 66 77}; with wviewer::over_graph true the `set fwd` line gives 1 (its only carve-outs are keysyms 100 and 98 under `$s & 4`); 77 is forwarded raw (only 109/100 go through wviewer::with_edit) as `xschem callback $W 2 x y 77 0 0 5`; key_filter never breaks. C: callback() strips bits above 12, Mod2Mask and LockMask, rstate also strips ShiftMask and Button1Mask -> ControlMask; handle_key_press: key_chord_has_binding(77, ControlMask) is 0 (no 'M' row in init_input_bindings, none in src/keybindings.csv, the user has no ~/.xschem/keybindings.csv); `case 'M'`, arm `rstate == ControlMask`, opens with `if(readonly_block()) break;` and has no waves_selected guard; readonly_block() is the tk_messageBox 'View is Read Only.'.

POINTER: the popup needs wviewer::over_graph true (current_win_path is this canvas AND mousex_snap/mousey_snap inside a full graphbb band; graphbb is written from the same band rects as the graph rects, no inset). Otherwise fwd stays 0, nothing is forwarded, no WaveViewer binding matches the chord (wviewer::install_default_binds has none for M; wviewer::case_pairs letters are d g n w e u b c q v), so it is a silent no-op. The C arm itself never looks at the pointer.

FAMILY, each arm read in handle_key_press / waves_selected / init_input_bindings: (a) Ctrl-Shift-M and Caps Lock + Ctrl-m -> `case 'M'` Ctrl arm -> readonly_block; (b) plain `s` with cadence_compat 1 -> `case 's'` arm `(rstate == 0) && cadence_compat` -> semaphore test -> readonly_block -> snapped_wire, no waves guard, no table row for s/0; (c) Alt-s / Super-s -> EQUAL_MODMASK arm -> okcancel 'reload from disk?' -> unselect_all, remove_symbols, load_schematic; (d) Ctrl-Alt-s -> `SET_MODMASK && (state & ControlMask)` -> saveas(NULL, SYMBOL) -> save_as_cellview_dialog (src/actions.c saveas); (e) Ctrl-Alt-t -> `rstate & ControlMask` arm, its waves_selected guard skips on SET_MODMASK -> new_schematic("create"); (f) Alt-b -> EQUAL_MODMASK arm cycles hide_symbols; (g) Alt-m -> forwarded inside with_edit (readonly 0, so readonly_block answers 0) -> EQUAL_MODMASK arm arms MENUSTART|MENUSTARTMOVE or move_objects(START). All unconditional once key_filter forwards.

A key in the border band, or one generated with no -x/-y, is therefore judged differently by the two sides.

missed.what: NumLock and the other masked bits will break the pure decision proc if it compares states exactly. The proposed matrix lists states {0,1,4,5,8,9,12,13,64,68} plus Lock {2,6,7} and no Mod2 state. With NumLock on, every key event carries Mod2 (16): bare `a` is 16, Ctrl-a is 20. Today's gate uses bit tests only, so it is NumLock-proof. The proc must normalise as callback() does (drop bits above 12, Mod2Mask, LockMask; then ShiftMask and Button1Mask for the reduced state) and decide on (case-mapped keysym, reduced state). The table derived from the C arms is small: forward only when the reduced state is 0 (all nine keysyms; 115 only without cadence_compat or via the reroute) or exactly Control (97 115 109 116 65 66; never 98 100 77). Acceptance legs must include 16, 17, 20, 21 and 256.

recommendation_holds:
With changes. The core holds: build A + B in one unit, Tcl only — a literal `bind WaveViewer <Control-Shift-Key-M>` default in wviewer::install_default_binds calling a new %W wrapper that ends in `wviewer::set_plot_mode invert $token` (TARGET subwindow, SW22), a case_pairs row `m {} <Control-Shift-Key-M>`, and key_filter deciding by chord so Ctrl+M and the Alt/Super chords are never forwarded. I found no other caller, profile or spec decision that this breaks, and no existing row pins Ctrl-Shift-M reaching C.

Changes the work order needs:
1. Accelerator: do not ship the guide data-menu/data-accel pair as recommended; it reddens GH6 of test_wave_grid on the display arm. Default to a data-seq-only guide row (literals 21 and 15, moved in GH0, BT09, BK10 and BX13 together), or extend `gh_find_entry` in the same commit if the user wants the accelerator shown.
2. Decision proc: it must normalise the state as callback() does (NumLock, Caps Lock, Shift, Button1) and decide on the reduced state; add NumLock legs to the matrix. Keep `graphkeys` byte-identical; if the `set fwd` line moves, BK01/BK02 move with it.
3. Border band and stale mirror: gate the forward on wviewer::strip_at_pixel_inset with the key event's own pixel (the btn2_filter precedent). That closes the geometry sibling from Tcl, so design D is not needed for this item.
4. Plain `s` in the Cadence profile is the user's daily profile (hdo-design sources cadence_style_rc) and should be closed in this unit. It can be done in Tcl by forwarding plain `s` as Ctrl+s (same swap arm, by reading), which avoids the C change to embedded graphs; the C guard remains the alternative the user can rule on. A red-first real-dispatch row for it is safe in test_wave_viewer.
5. Fences: put the real-key red-first rows in test_wave_viewer (the only suite with the tk_messageBox stub, and it sends -x/-y).
